Sampled HR@10 measures performance against the pinned 99 negatives; it does not establish full-catalog ranking quality, and sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings ([Krichene and Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)). Preserve users, candidates and evaluation seed across comparisons. For uncertainty, adapt [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/): resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical sampled indices for both models; calculate category hit-rate differences and their equal-weight macro-average over four categories. Report the observed difference and a 95% bootstrap interval. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals are conditional on fixed candidates and fitted models; they exclude candidate-sampling and training variability.

Repeated validation-driven selection can overfit even without accessing test labels ([Cawley and Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Predeclare search spaces, checkpoint rules, comparison families and budgets; retain all trial results. Where permitted, repeat the entire selection procedure under equal budgets and report winner variability, rather than only rerunning the winning configuration. With training seed fixed at 42, characterize permitted search-order variability explicitly. Bootstrapping already-selected winners does not remove selection bias; validation conclusions remain exploratory until independent held-out evaluation.

For attribution, compare baseline, loss-only, ungated text fusion, repeated-support gating, and auxiliary supervision through controlled additions and removals. Hold backbone, data, candidates and training protocol constant; compare gated versus ungated fusion directly and auxiliary supervision on/off within the same architecture. Match total GPU-seconds, including tuning and failed trials; equal trial counts can conceal unequal costs. Budget-sensitive comparisons follow [hyperparameter-search benchmarking principles](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v13/bergstra12a.html). Report per-category effects alongside macro results; avoid attributing combined gains to individual components without those controls.
